## The level is the scope

Delivery for large and high-value pieces runs in four named levels, and the level is not a label — it is the scope of work. Curbside stops at the curb. Threshold stops at the first dry covered spot inside. Room of choice carries the boxed item to the room you name and stops there. White glove — the level this service runs — finishes the job in the room: protected carry-in on a surveyed path, placement to your plan, unpacking, full assembly, a joint inspection with the condition noted on the delivery record, and every piece of packaging out with the crew. The level is chosen and written into your flat-rate quote before the truck rolls, across the full published footprint — all 71 areas, both branches. Two more federal facts shape the service: on an interstate move, full value protection is the default liability level (released value, at 60 cents per pound per article, applies only if you sign for it), and any item worth more than $100 per pound must be listed on the shipping documents — which is why a white-glove job here starts with an item list, not a truck.

## Questions, answered

What is white-glove delivery?

White-glove delivery means the item crosses the threshold: brought in on a planned route, set in its final position, packaging removed and condition verified with you before the crew leaves — never left at a curb. It is the top level of final-mile delivery: room of choice plus unpacking, inspection with the recipient, and packaging and debris removal.

How are items protected for a white-glove delivery?

Each piece is assessed on its own — weight, fragile points, finish and value at risk — and the protection is matched to the piece: items travel fully covered in padded blankets and sealed with clear stretch wrap, or in a custom crate built around the piece when the piece demands it.

What kinds of items does white-glove delivery cover?

Antiques, art, pianos and instruments are the everyday work of this service, along with high-value and fragile freight generally. The heavy examples the pages name are a safe, a piano and medical equipment — pieces of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs, which join the SIR plan before they move.

What happens with a heavy white-glove delivery?

A high-value delivery that weighs 1,500 to 3,500 lbs — a safe, a piano, medical equipment — is surveyed and floor-checked to L/360 under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol like any SIR move, so placement never becomes an improvisation at your door.

What are the delivery levels, and where does white glove sit?

Curbside (left at the curb or driveway); threshold (carried inside the first door, garage or lobby); room of choice (carried to the room the recipient picks, no unpacking); room of choice with packaging removal; and white glove at the top (room of choice plus unpacking, inspection with the recipient, and packaging and debris removal). Some providers add assembly or installation above white glove. The ladder is industry vocabulary — no regulator defines these names.

What should you confirm before you book?

Confirm in writing, whichever level you are buying: the endpoint (curb, first door, or a named room — and whether stairs are included); unpacking; packaging removal and what it excludes; assembly and installation; the appointment, who must be present, and whether a signature is required; inspection at signing, with condition recorded before the paperwork is signed; and the failed-delivery answer — what happens, and who pays, if the item cannot be carried in.

Does white-glove delivery include assembly?

Sometimes in the industry — and only when it is agreed. Industry descriptions list assembly among the things white-glove service may include, and the scope depends on the carrier and the agreement, so it has to be confirmed before booking. On our side the answer is plain: assembly and installation are not part of our published scope. If a delivery turns on either, settle it with us when the job is scoped.

Is debris removal included with a delivery?

Often at the white-glove tier, but it should still be confirmed before booking — and confirm what the words cover. Removing the delivered item's own packaging is one service; hauling away the old item it replaces is another, and the second is not implied by the first. Our published practice covers the delivered item's packaging; haul-away of old items is not published as part of our service.

Can a white-glove delivery be scheduled?

Yes — appointment-based delivery is the norm for freight of any size. White-glove services commonly run on scheduled appointment windows, and retail freight deliveries are typically arranged on an appointment with a signature required. Our deliveries are arranged by appointment too; no fixed window length is published — the appointment is set when the job is scoped and quoted.

Is white-glove delivery available for residences?

Yes. White-glove service is frequently used for residential freight shipments — furniture, appliances, electronics, medical equipment and other big or high-value pieces. Our deliveries run to homes as well as to offices, industrial sites and retail spaces, dispatched from the Winchester and Martinsburg branches. A residence with stairs or a heavy piece is exactly the delivery to confirm in detail before the day.

Why does white-glove delivery cost more than curbside?

Because the service is different work, not a different label. White-glove pricing carries two-person teams, the scheduling coordination of an appointment, the extra time to carry, place, unpack and inspect, and the liability management of handling heavy or high-value freight inside the building. A curbside price stops at the curb — and hands you the carry, the placement and the stair risk.

What should I check before I sign for a delivery?

Check the item in its final position before the paperwork is signed: finish, corners, doors and drawers, and whether it is complete. Note any damage on the delivery documents, not after the crew has gone. Our crews verify condition with you before they leave.

How is white-glove delivery quoted?

Pieces are surveyed in advance and the job is quoted at one flat rate, agreed in writing before dispatch — Get My Flat Rate Quote, Short (Quick Quote) by default or Detailed Project with From, To, and What's moving preserved between them. The quote reviews the full scope of the job — the pieces, the distance, the manpower and the equipment. hourly pricing is available when a client asks for it. Or call +1-540-422-2153.

# Office Moving
Office moving — workstations, files and equipment. Complete office relocations from The Flat Rate Movers, quoted flat and agreed in writing: moved in a planned order so your team can sit down and work at the new address. Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free!

Get My Flat Rate Quote (#/quote)

[Image: The Flat Rate Movers logo — company brand image, not a job photo.]The Flat Rate Movers logo — company brand image, not a job photo.

## Office moving, defined

Office moving from The Flat Rate Movers is a complete office relocation — desks and workstations, files and records runs, and office equipment — planned as a sequence with you, staged when the dates require it, and placed at the new address in the order your team needs to work.

## Planned, staged, placed

An office move is a sequence, not a pile. We plan the order with you — what leaves first, what arrives first, and where each workstation, file run and piece of equipment lands. That planning is what keeps downtime short: what moves first, what moves last, and what your team needs working on day one are settled before move day, not during it.

Workstations and furniture — desks and workstations moved as a planned set. Files and records runs — file runs kept in order so they land usable. Office equipment — the equipment the office runs on, handled as part of the sequence. Industrial offices — office areas inside plants, warehouses and industrial facilities, moved with the site itself planned first: access, floor space, staging and equipment handling.

## Packing, staging and the freight behind the move

Full or partial packing for offices is part of this service, and staging at our warehouse covers the gap when the dates do not line up neatly — then placement at the new site runs in the order your team needs it. Our warehouse and transload operation is the staging base behind office and industrial moves: freight and equipment handled between truck, container and warehouse, on the same job, under one roof. For bigger commercial jobs the same chain carries container loading and unloading, transloading and final-mile delivery. Commercial equipment, safes and sensitive devices up to 3,500 lbs move under SIR and the KIM-GS Protocol — route surveyed, floor checked to L/360, load spread and protected.

## Who this is for

Office managers, business owners, and facility teams moving a professional office, a shop office, or an industrial office inside a plant, warehouse, or industrial facility — where access, floor space, staging, and equipment handling must be planned around the site itself. The wider commercial category — shops and commercial spaces, government offices and military households on the same flat-rate-in-writing basis — lives on the Commercial Moving page linked below.

## Workstations come apart in one order — and the power dies first

A cubicle system is engineered to disassemble, in a fixed order: devices off, mounted components down, panels out, connector rails detached, frame last. Before any of it, the circuit feeding the panels' power whips is de-energized — panels never move on a live whip. The survey names the system on your floor, because every brand connects differently: Steelcase's spring-loaded clips press and lift, other systems run on rods, bolts, or gravity locks, and the wrong assumption costs hours on your clock. Timed honestly, a standard two-panel station is 30 to 45 minutes of teardown for two people — the known quantity the whole schedule is built from. Every part is color-labeled to your destination floor plan, panels stack in rebuild sequence, and the finish line is not an empty truck: it is your people at working desks on the next business day.

## Questions, answered

### What is an industrial offices move?
An industrial offices move is the office area inside a plant, warehouse or industrial facility — plant offices, warehouse offices and facility administration areas — as distinct from a commercial office in an office building. It covers office furniture and equipment, files and fixtures, and the packing, protection and placement that goes with them, moved at one flat rate in writing from Winchester, VA and Martinsburg, WV — the same flat-rate standard as every other move, planned for the site it sits in. Where an office-area item is high-mass (1,500 to 3,500 lbs), it moves under SIR and the KIM-GS Protocol with L/360 floor-deflection analysis.

### How is this different from a standard office move?
The setting. A standard office move is a commercial office; an industrial offices move is the office area inside a plant, warehouse or industrial facility — same flat-rate standard, planned for the site it sits in.

### What about heavy equipment in the office area?
Any item of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs moves under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol, with floor-deflection analysis to L/360, before anything is lifted.

### Can this run alongside warehouse or project work?
Yes. Industrial & Commercial Services covers warehouse and distribution, commercial relocation and logistics, FF&E installation and project support, and flexible workforce deployment — priced per job, with no required contract duration.

### How do I get the quote?
Get My Flat Rate Quote — Short Quick Quote by default, Detailed Project one toggle away, preserving From, To and What’s moving. Phone +1-540-422-2153, email ratemovers@gmail.com.

### The move, step by step

Step | What happens |

1. Survey | The office area, its contents, and the site are walked and scoped — dock access, move hours, security protocol, and parking and permits are captured as quote inputs. |

2. Phased plan | What leaves first, what arrives first, and where each workstation, file run and piece of equipment lands is planned around production and site access. |

3. Pack and label | Office furniture, equipment, files and fixtures are packed, protected and labeled to the plan. |

4. Sequenced move | The move runs in the planned sequence at the one flat rate agreed in writing before move day — hourly pricing is available when a client asks for it. |

5. Install and place | Workstations, furniture and equipment are placed where the plan puts them at the destination. |

6. Verify | Placement is checked against the plan with the client. |

7. Close-out | The job is closed out with the site working again on day one. |

### Terms that shape an industrial office move

Industrial office
The office area inside a plant, warehouse or industrial facility — plant offices, warehouse offices and facility administration areas — as distinct from a commercial office in an office building.
Quote inputs
The site facts confirmed before a flat rate is quoted: dock access, move hours, security protocol, and parking and permits.
High-mass item
Any single item of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs. In an office area it moves under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol, with floor-deflection analysis to L/360, before anything is lifted.
L/360
The floor-deflection limit used in the SIR check: the floor span divided by 360. The floor is checked against it before a high-mass move is planned.
Flat rate, in writing
Every job is reviewed in full — scope, distance, manpower and equipment — and priced at one flat rate, agreed in writing before move day. The standard price is one flat rate; hourly pricing is available when a client asks for it. Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free!

## What government moving is

Government moving is the relocation of government offices and public-sector workplaces — workstations, files and office equipment moved in a planned sequence around the agency's schedule and site requirements, surveyed in advance, documented, and quoted at one flat rate in writing before move day, so approvals and budgets work from a fixed number.

This hub is the government-only page for the service. The shared military & government page, the Winchester and Martinsburg government branch pages, and the household-goods requirements article below carry it in depth. Office areas, records, files and equipment move on a planned, sequenced schedule so the office is working again on day one, with industrial-office and warehouse staging support from the company's own transload operation behind the job. The written quote is produced from the Detailed Project form — project type, dates, rooms or facility size, and access at both ends — the format approvals and budgets actually need. No contracts, clearances, or discounts are claimed for this service.

## A government office move, step by step

1. Survey — the office, its contents and both ends' access are surveyed before anything is priced.

2. Phased plan — the move is planned in phases around the office's operating hours and deadlines, and quoted at one flat rate in writing.

3. Pack and label — workstations, files and office equipment are packed and labeled to the plan — handled as planned runs, not loose loads.

4. Sequenced move — contents move in the planned sequence, with industrial-office and warehouse staging support from our own transload operation behind the job.

5. Install and place — each workstation, file run and piece of equipment is placed where the plan puts it at the new address.

6. Verify — placement is verified against the plan with the office before close-out.

7. Close-out — the move closes out on the written flat rate agreed before move day — the office is working again on day one.

## Building requirements, confirmed before move day

Freight-elevator reservation — whether the building's freight elevator must be reserved, and for which windows, is confirmed as a quote input. Dock access — loading-dock availability and any dock rules at both ends are confirmed before the sequence is set. Move hours — the hours the building allows moving work are confirmed and the plan is sequenced inside them. Advance notice — how far ahead the building must be notified is confirmed at quote stage, not discovered on move day. Security protocol — the site's security protocol is confirmed as a quote input; the move is planned around the building's stated rules. Parking and permits — where trucks may park and stage, and any permits that takes, are confirmed before move day.

Home bases in Winchester, VA and Martinsburg, WV — established June 2010 — cover Frederick County, Berkeley County, Loudoun County, Jefferson County, Morgan County, the Shenandoah Valley and the Eastern Panhandle. Heavy and sensitive pieces are covered on the same job: safes, medical devices, cryogenic equipment and antiques from 1,500 to 3,500 lbs move under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol with an L/360 floor check.

MILITARY MOVING — WINCHESTER VA & MARTINSBURG WV

# Military Moving
Moving services for U.S. military households and service members relocating to or from the Winchester and Martinsburg area, from The Flat Rate Movers. Relocations run on orders and deadlines, not on convenience — dates are planned around your reporting timeline, and the move is quoted at one flat rate in writing before move day. Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free!

Get My Flat Rate Quote (#/quote)

[Image: The Flat Rate Movers logo — company brand image, not a job photo.]The Flat Rate Movers logo — company brand image, not a job photo.

## What military moving is

Military moving is the relocation of U.S. military households and service members to or from the Winchester and Martinsburg area: whole-home moves with full, partial or fragile-only packing and unpacking, heavy pieces planned under SIR and the KIM-GS Protocol, dates set around the reporting timeline, and one flat rate agreed in writing before move day.

This hub is the military-only page for the service. The shared military & government page, the Winchester and Martinsburg military branch pages, and the household-goods requirements article below carry it in depth. The service runs local, regional and long-distance on I-81, I-66 and I-70. It is a direct-hire service for military households: the company is not assigned moves through the Defense Personal Property System, and claims no transportation-service-provider status, no program participation, no government contract and no clearance for this service.

## A military household move, step by step

1. Survey and written quote — the household is surveyed and the move is quoted at one flat rate, agreed in writing before move day — dates planned around your reporting timeline.

2. Room-by-room packing — full, partial or fragile-only packing, room by room, against an itemized inventory.

3. Sequenced loading — the load is sequenced for the planned route — local, regional or long-distance on I-81, I-66 and I-70.

4. Transport on the planned route — the household moves on the route the plan set, at the flat rate agreed — hourly pricing is available when a client asks for it.

5. Room-by-room unloading and placement — goods are unloaded and placed room by room at the new home, not dropped at the door.

6. Closing walkthrough — the move closes with a walkthrough; heavy pieces — safes, pianos, equipment — were surveyed under SIR/KIM-GS with an L/360 floor check where the 1,500–3,500 lb band applies.

## Reference — how the military moving system works

General information about the system around a military move — not a description of this company's services. PCS orders — Permanent Change of Station orders move a service member to a new duty station; the orders carry the report date the whole move is planned backward from. Transportation office and DPS — households are counseled at their installation transportation office or self-counsel in the Defense Personal Property System (DPS) at move.mil; that office and the orders — not a mover — set the move's requirements: dates, allowances and paperwork. Government-arranged move (DP3) — under the Defense Personal Property Program, a counseled shipment is booked to a transportation service provider (TSP), which surveys, packs, transports and delivers it; the household does not hire that mover. Personally procured move (PPM) — the route where the member arranges the move themselves — formerly called a DITY move — authorized in advance through the transportation office (DD Form 2278) and reimbursed against the government's constructed cost, with certified weight tickets kept as evidence; a household on this route hires its mover directly. Weight allowance — household goods weight allowances are set by the Joint Travel Regulations and vary by pay grade and dependency status; your own allowance is confirmed in counseling — plan the inventory against it, because weight beyond the allowance is the household's cost risk. Start with your own requirements: confirm dates, allowances and paperwork with your orders and your transportation or HR office first; then bring us the dates and the inventory, and we plan the move to fit the window you have been given.

## Who it is for

Service members and military families relocating to or from the Winchester and Martinsburg area. The service's household-goods article also addresses government employees and government contractors planning an HHG (household goods) move from the area: the move is planned around your orders and dates, with an itemized inventory and one flat rate in writing that approvals and budgets can actually use. Heavy & sensitive, covered: safes, medical devices, cryogenic equipment and antiques of 1,500–3,500 lbs move under SIR/KIM-GS with an L/360 floor check, and full, partial or fragile-only packing is available.

### Route 81 Corridor Moving and Dispatch

🛣️ THE CORRIDOR PAGE

# Route 81: our road, our advantage.

We live on Interstate 81. With bases in Winchester, VA and Martinsburg, WV — where I-81 meets I-66 and I-70 — we dispatch faster, route smarter, and keep flat rates honest across the Shenandoah Valley and the Eastern Panhandle.

Quote a Route 81 move (#/quote)

[Image: Farm country in the Shenandoah Valley, Virginia — fields, fences and farm buildings with the Blue Ridge beyond]Farm country in the Shenandoah Valley, VA — the valley floor I-81 runs through on its 325-mile Virginia segment, the longest in any state · Photo: Pollinator, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons

Tap a stop — north to south on I-81

## The corridor, stop by stop

## Three interstates, one dispatch

### I-81 — The Spine
North–south through Martinsburg, Winchester, Harrisonburg, Staunton, Lexington and Roanoke. Our daily working road for Valley moves and long-distance runs.

- Local & regional home moves
- Long-distance south & north
- Heavy-asset runs with SIR planning

### I-66 — To NoVA & DC
East from the Valley through Front Royal toward Northern Virginia and Washington, DC. The route for relocations between the Valley and the metro.

- Valley ↔ Northern Virginia moves
- Commercial & office relocations
- Final-mile delivery into the metro

### I-70 — To Maryland & the Ports
Through Hagerstown and Frederick toward Baltimore — and the freight path that connects our transload work to the Port of Virginia network.

- Container loading & unloading
- Transloading at hub points
- Export freight toward port

### Why the corridor matters to your price

Hourly movers charge for every mile the clock runs. We quote flat — and because our crews start on the corridor instead of driving hours to reach it, there's less deadhead time baked into your price. Fewer wasted miles, tighter arrival windows, one agreed number.

Get the flat number → (#/quote)

### What Route 81 moving includes

Dispatch from Winchester, VA (I-81 meets I-66) and Martinsburg, WV (I-81 with the I-70 connection): local and regional home moves, long-distance south and north, heavy-asset runs with SIR planning, transloading at hub points, and export freight toward the port — all on I-81 as the spine, with I-66 to Northern Virginia and DC, and I-70 to Maryland and the ports.

### Who Route 81 is for

Valley and Panhandle households and businesses whose move starts on the corridor, and long-distance customers whose run follows I-81, I-66, or I-70 — where crews starting on the corridor mean less deadhead time and tighter arrival windows.

### The three corridors — highway geography (domain reference)

This table describes the roads themselves — where they run and where they join. It is geography, not coverage: a town a highway passes is not a place we serve unless it appears in the footprint table below.

Corridor | The road | Our dispatch anchor |

I-81 — the spine | About 855 miles north–south along the Appalachian spine from Tennessee to New York; the Virginia segment runs about 325 miles up the Shenandoah Valley — Martinsburg, Winchester, Harrisonburg, Staunton, Lexington and Roanoke, north to south — paralleling US 11, running with I-64 between Lexington and Staunton, and carrying, per VDOT, the highest per-capita truck volume in Virginia. | Both branches sit on it: Winchester, VA and Martinsburg, WV. |

I-66 — to Northern Virginia & DC | About 76 miles east from its western terminus at I-81 near Middletown, VA (I-81 exit 300), through Front Royal (US 340 / US 522), across the Blue Ridge at Manassas Gap, to Washington, DC — the only Interstate running west from Washington into Northern Virginia. | Winchester, at the I-81 × I-66 junction. |

I-70 — to Maryland & the ports | Crosses I-81 at Hagerstown, MD and runs through Frederick toward Baltimore — the freight path that connects our transload work to the port network. | Martinsburg, on I-81 with the I-70 connection. |

🏭 INDUSTRIAL & COMMERCIAL SERVICES

# Trained, supervised moving and warehouse teams for industrial and commercial work.

The Flat Rate Movers provides trained, supervised moving and warehouse teams to support military shipments, regular household-goods shipments, warehouse operations, and residential jobs where additional manpower is needed. Services are priced per job with no required contract duration. The service's workforce layer, Specialized Workforce Labor, carries workforce deployment coverage in all 48 contiguous states, quoted per job — distinct from the branches' moving footprint, whose service areas load from the GeoJSON below, by branch. This service is for project managers, operations managers, warehouse managers, logistics coordinators, general contractors, commercial furniture dealers, healthcare facilities managers, and other industrial and commercial buyers who need planned or overflow manpower, confirmed before dispatch.

## SUPPORT WE CAN PROVIDE

### Military and regular HHG loading / unloading
Military shipments and regular household-goods shipments, loaded and unloaded by trained, supervised teams.

### APU / driver crew support
Crew provided when additional service labor is needed, including driver-meet support on site.

### Warehouse load-outs and inbound unloads
Warehouse load-outs, inbound unloads, trailer loading and offloading, and warehouse organization.

### Vault / container handling
Vault and container handling, warehouse organization, inventory, sorting, labeling, and pallet work.

### Residential driver-meet jobs
Residential jobs where the team meets the driver on site.

### Rush, overflow, and short-notice manpower
Peak-season, overflow, weekend, vacation-coverage, and emergency-response support, including rapid / same-day deployment where the job allows.

## Ocean containers, PODS, transloading, restacking, packing

### Ocean containers
Ocean container unloading and loading, container support, cross-docking, and container handling in the warehouse and transload operation.

### PODS
PODS loading and unloading, with packing, protection, and placement planned for the container, not improvised on site.

### Transloading & restacking
Transloading between truck, container, and warehouse, restacking for safe transport and storage, and warehouse cleanup and project support.

## HOW WE OPERATE

- Self-managed teams — not individual temp labor

- In-house trained moving and warehouse crews

- Crew size matched to each job

- Job-by-job pricing with no required duration

- Planned and overflow support

- Scope and price confirmed before dispatch

## Standard Job Pricing

Unload — $8.00 CWT — Warehouse, military or regular HHG unload.

Load — $10.00 CWT — Warehouse load-out, origin service or regular HHG load.

APU — $12.00 CWT — Crew provided when additional service labor is needed.

Residential / Driver Meet — $400–$425 per man — Residential job where the team meets the driver on site.

Rates are quoted per job and may be adjusted for unusual scope, special equipment, travel, after-hours requirements, or other conditions agreed to before dispatch. These are per-job industrial and commercial rates for this service — they are not the residential flat-rate moving price, which is quoted separately, in writing, for a household move.

### Terms used on this page

CWT
Hundredweight — 100 lb. The standard weight unit in freight and household-goods rating; unload and load pricing scales with shipment weight, not clock time.
HHG
Household goods. Military and regular HHG shipments are loaded and unloaded by trained, supervised teams under this service.
FF&E
Furniture, fixtures and equipment — the installable contents of a commercial or hospitality project, handled here as installation and project support: receiving and warehousing coordination, installation, punch lists and closeout.
Punch list
The documented list of incomplete or deficient items to correct before a project is accepted as complete.
Deployment need
The reason a team is engaged: Planned Projects, Overflow Demand, Peak Season, Weekend Support, Vacation Coverage, or Emergency Response — including rapid and same-day deployment where the job allows.
Markets served
Warehousing & Distribution; Manufacturing; Transportation & Logistics; Retail Distribution; Third-Party Logistics; Healthcare Facilities; Commercial Furniture Dealers; Corporate Offices; General Contractors; Educational Institutions; Hospitality & Hotel Renovations.

## Training & Crew Standards

Teams are trained in-house for HHG moving, warehouse handling, property care, and jobsite conduct. Site-specific rules, equipment restrictions, and required certifications are confirmed before dispatch.

What does the Industrial & Commercial service provide, and how is it priced?

The Flat Rate Movers provides trained, supervised moving and warehouse teams to support military shipments, regular household-goods shipments, warehouse operations, and residential jobs where additional manpower is needed. ### Senior Moving

SENIOR MOVING — WINCHESTER VA & MARTINSBURG WV

# Senior Moving — Winchester VA & Martinsburg WV.
Senior moving from The Flat Rate Movers, for seniors downsizing, transitioning to assisted or independent living, or relocating closer to family, across the Shenandoah Valley and Eastern Panhandle. Flat-rate moves quoted in writing — one flat price agreed before move day, hourly pricing is available when a client asks for it. Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free! Senior moving is also listed as Senior Advocacy Logistics.

Get My Flat Rate Quote (#/quote)

[Image: The Flat Rate Movers logo — company brand image, not a job photo.]The Flat Rate Movers logo — company brand image, not a job photo.

## Who it is for

This service is for seniors and their families: seniors downsizing after years in one home, seniors transitioning to assisted or independent living, seniors relocating closer to family, and families coordinating a senior move — including adult children coordinating from out of town.

## What it includes

Packing support for senior moves, including fragile items and keepsakes. The free video-walkthrough survey room: film only — never lift, move, open, or climb anything heavy or locked — with a human-made estimate. One flat price agreed in writing before move day.

If a senior move involves a very heavy item — a high-mass asset in the 1,500–3,500 lb range — that item moves under Structural Integrity Relocation (SIR), with floor deflection analysis to L/360, as part of the same flat-rate move. SIR is not claimed for senior moves generally; it applies only where such an asset is actually involved.

## How it works

1. Get My Flat Rate Quote — Short (Quick Quote) or Detailed Project, switching in place with From, To, and What's moving preserved.

2. Add the free video walkthrough if wanted — the survey room covers main living areas, bedroom and personal rooms, and keepsakes and fragile items, one prompt per screen, filmed only.

3. The estimate is human-made. The move is quoted flat in writing before move day.

What if the senior move includes a very heavy item?

## Who it is for

This service is for warehouse and distribution operations and the buyers who plan their moves: warehouse operators, distribution and 3PL operations, manufacturers, and project managers, contractors, and operations buyers planning a warehouse move, a warehouse load-out, or inbound unloading work.

## What it includes

Warehouse and distribution moves, warehouse load-outs and inbound unloads, transload staging, and restacking — carried out by supervised warehouse teams. A warehouse load-out is the loading out of a warehouse; an inbound unload is the unloading of inbound freight on arrival. Work is planned around the site itself: access, floor space, staging, and equipment handling, so the move fits the operation instead of interrupting it.

If a warehouse move involves a very heavy item — a high-mass asset in the 1,500–3,500 lb range — that item moves under Structural Integrity Relocation (SIR), with floor deflection analysis to L/360, as part of the same flat-rate job. SIR is not claimed for warehouse moves generally; it applies only where such an asset is actually involved.

## How it works

1. Get My Flat Rate Quote — Short (Quick Quote) or Detailed Project, switching in place with From, To, and What's moving preserved.

2. The job is scoped around the site — access, floor space, staging, and equipment handling — and quoted flat per job, agreed before dispatch.

3. Supervised warehouse teams carry out the load-out, inbound unload, staging, or restack, with no required contract duration.

## Standard Job Pricing

Unload $8.00/CWT, Load $10.00/CWT, APU $12.00/CWT, Residential/Driver Meet $400–$425 per man. Quoted per job, adjustable for scope, equipment, travel, and after-hours agreed before dispatch.

[Image: The Flat Rate Movers logo — company brand image, not a job photo.]The Flat Rate Movers logo — company brand image, not a job photo.

## Who it is for

This service is for the people who move freight through ports and need the inland link to hold: importers and distributors receiving regular overseas shipments; retail and e-commerce businesses turning stock over fast; 3PLs, freight forwarders, and brokers who need a reliable local partner for the warehouse workflow; manufacturers receiving components and raw materials; warehouses and distribution centers facing floor-loaded arrivals, multi-container days, and overflow or surge; and project cargo owners with heavy or oversized loads. The buyer is usually an operations person — a warehouse or logistics manager, a project manager — buying on dock reliability, pace, sequencing, and communication.

## What transloading is

Transloading is unloading plus immediate reload into domestic equipment: typically a 40ft ocean container's cargo restacked into 53ft domestic trailers, so the ocean box returns near the port and the domestic trailer carries the inland leg. It gives the shipper control over routing, speed to multiple markets, and capacity use.

The words around it, as the industry uses them:

- Unloading (devanning / destuffing) — removing cargo from an ocean container at a warehouse or container freight station, then sorting and staging it for delivery. "Destuffing" is the same operation; the word is standard on Asian and UK trade documents.

- Cross-docking — freight that never enters storage: it touches the dock floor for hours, not days, then leaves on outbound LTL or FTL the same shift. A transload is often done as a cross-dock move, but it can also include a few days of storage between legs.

- Deconsolidation (decon) — breaking a consolidated container apart by destination, purchase order, or SKU: the step that turns one inbound box into many outbound loads.

- Drayage — the short-range move, usually 100 miles or less, that carries a released container from its port of arrival to a nearby warehouse or storage facility. It is a step in the chain described below; this page does not state who performs it (see Questions, answered).

- IPI vs transload — under IPI (inland point intermodal), the original ocean container continues inland to the destination. Under transloading, cargo transfers to domestic equipment in the first mile, which adds control and visibility and makes it easier to pivot between rail and truck.

## How a transload runs

The chain, step by step, with the company's verified steps in it:

1. Pre-arrival planning — outbound routing, destination addresses, load plan, and equipment count confirmed before the vessel arrives; the transload appointment booked before the container leaves the terminal.

2. Port release and the short move in — the container is picked up at the terminal as soon as it is released and delivered to the transload and warehouse facility inside the ocean carrier's free time.

3. Devanning, count, and inspection — the container is unloaded, floor-loaded or palletized; freight is counted and inspected; damage is photographed and reported the same day, in writing, so the buyer sees actual cargo condition before it travels inland.

4. Rework — cargo is palletized if needed, shrink-wrapped, labeled, sorted by purchase order, SKU, or destination, and segregated for multi-destination loads.

5. Restacking into domestic equipment — cargo is restacked into 53ft trailers (a 40ft container becomes about 20 pallet positions; a 20ft about 10) or staged for storage.

6. Inland dispatch — trailers depart same-day or next-morning for warehouses, distribution centers, retail partners, or final customers, as FTL, LTL, or split delivery.

7. Empty return — the ocean container returns to the terminal immediately after devanning, before per-diem charges start.

8. Final mile — last-leg delivery to stores, offices, homes, and job sites by appointment, through the company's verified final-mile delivery service.

The company's own published steps sit inside this chain: receive, unload, count, sort by destination, stage, and build outbound (container deconsolidation reference), and quoted, surveyed, packed, loaded, transloaded, delivered, and verified placement (logistics event protocol).

## The cost-avoidance terms

These are industry terms, stated here as domain facts — they are the reason transload speed matters:

- Free time and last free day (LFD) — every container has free time at the terminal and with the carrier. Past the last free day, charges start.

- Demurrage — the charge for a box sitting at the terminal past free time.

- Detention (per-diem) — the charge for a box kept outside the terminal past free time.

- Chassis — the wheeled frame a container rides on for the short move. Chassis sourcing, shortages, and tri-axle chassis for overweight boxes are routine cost and schedule variables.

- The overweight alternative — where a container genuinely cannot be permitted to destination, transloading its cargo into domestic trailers removes the container weight from the equation; for some lanes that is cheaper than permitting even when a permit is available.

Moving a box inside free time is the entire cost-avoidance game. Warehouse storage is cheaper than port demurrage, which is why importers use the short move to a warehouse when congestion makes long-range scheduling unreliable.

## Questions, answered

What is transloading?

Unloading an ocean container plus immediate reload into domestic equipment — typically a 40ft ocean container's cargo restacked into 53ft domestic trailers — so the ocean box returns near the port and the domestic trailer carries the inland leg.

How is transloading different from cross-docking and deconsolidation?

Cross-docking means freight never enters storage: it leaves on outbound LTL or FTL the same shift. Deconsolidation means breaking one consolidated container apart by destination, purchase order, or SKU into many outbound loads. A transload often includes one or both, plus storage between legs where needed.

What do free time, demurrage, and detention mean for my shipment?

Free time is the window before charges start; the last free day (LFD) ends it. Past LFD, the terminal charges demurrage for a box sitting at the terminal, and the carrier charges detention (per-diem) for a box kept outside the terminal. Moving the box inside free time — and transloading promptly — is how those charges are avoided.

What if my container is overweight?

Where a container genuinely cannot be permitted to destination, transloading its cargo into domestic trailers removes the container weight from the equation; for some lanes that is cheaper than permitting even when a permit is available. Scope and pricing are quoted per job.

Which branch serves my transload — Winchester or Martinsburg?

Winchester transloads are served by The Flat Rate Movers (116 W Piccadilly St Suite 11, Winchester VA 22601; Mon-Fri 8-6, Sat 8-4, Sun 9-4). Martinsburg transloads are served by Flat Rate Movers Martinsburg WV (736 Williamsport Pike Suite 2, Martinsburg WV 25404; Mon-Fri 9-6, Sat 9-4, Sun 9-4) on its own page. Hours, names, and ratings differ by branch and are listed separately above.

How is a transloading job priced?

Container transloading jobs are quoted per job, agreed in writing before dispatch. No per-container or per-CWT container rate is stated on this page.

Does this page cover reefer, bonded, or customs work?

No. Reefer and cold-chain handling, bonded warehouse or foreign-trade zone operation, and customs brokerage are not claimed on this page. Container jobs are quoted per job — send the job details through Get My Flat Rate Quote (#/quote).

What if the load includes a very heavy item?

If a transload involves a high-mass asset in the 1,500–3,500 lb range, that asset moves under Structural Integrity Relocation (SIR), with floor deflection analysis to L/360, as part of the same flat-rate job. SIR is not claimed for transloading generally; it applies only where such an asset is actually involved.

How do I get a flat rate quote for a transload?

Get My Flat Rate Quote (#/quote) — Short (Quick Quote) by default, or Detailed Project, switching in place with From, To, and What's moving preserved. The pill button reads "Get a flat rate quote".

## Where this work sits in the chain

Every container that reaches the Valley rides the same chain: vessel to a Norfolk marine terminal, crane to a double-stack Norfolk Southern train, rail through Manassas and along I-66 to Front Royal, a lift at the Virginia Inland Port, and a truck for the last regional miles. The inland port — 161 acres at the I-81 and I-66 junction, owned by the Virginia Port Authority, a U.S. Customs-designated port of entry — pulls the seaport 220 miles inland, and this service is the dock-and-road work at that end of the chain: unloading and devanning, sorting, restacking and palletizing, cross-docking inside the appointment, freight rework when a load arrives wrong, and the regional truck legs arranged per job. Two distinctions run the work. Transloading opens the box — the cargo itself changes units — where intermodal shipping never does; and cross-docking is a race through the dock, in and out inside the day, where a transload is measured by a finished, reloaded unit. The service covers the full published footprint — all 71 areas, both branches — and every job is quoted per job, in writing, before work begins.

# Moving and Storage — Winchester VA & Martinsburg WV

## Leased storage, on stated terms

Storage is leased. We provide leased storage for any type of items — including containers, household goods, and machines such as robotic arms. Minimum stay is 30 days. Customers can access their stored items while stored. Lease terms vary.

## Who it is for

This service is for anyone whose two dates stopped lining up: closing-gap movers whose sale closes on one date and purchase on another; renovators whose work finishes after move-out; downsizers and estate transitions sorting what fits; staged movers moving in phases; seasonal and temporary-housing holds; commercial staging between leases or mid-build-out; and long-distance moves with a delivery window on either end.

## What it includes

The move side, as published on the residential page (#/residential): whole-home and apartment moves of every size; loading, transport and unloading; furniture protection and careful placement; disassembly and reassembly of standard furniture, planned up front; full, partial, or fragile-only packing, plus unpacking at the other end; white-glove care for antiques and high-value pieces; custom crates when a piece needs more than padding.

The storage interval: items held in leased storage between move-out and move-in, then redelivered and placed room by room. Minimum stay is 30 days. Customers can access their stored items while stored. Lease terms vary. Storage is quoted per job, monthly, or by volume. If a move involves a very heavy item — a high-mass asset in the 1,500–3,500 lb range — that item moves under Structural Integrity Relocation (SIR) (#/heavy), with floor deflection analysis to L/360, as part of the same flat-rate move.

This is not the warehouse floor used for freight staging and transloading. That floor — industrial-commercial warehouse space, load-outs, inbound unloads, container handling — is a different service: Industrial & Commercial Services (#/industrial-commercial-services). Moving and storage holds your items between move-out and move-in; freight staging moves freight onward. The two are never blurred.

Specialty pieces move under their own categories — piano and antique moving, gun-safe moving under SIR, custom crating — and are cross-referenced here, never duplicated. Ask about a specialty piece when you request a quote.

## How it works

1. Get My Flat Rate Quote — Short (Quick Quote) or Detailed Project, switching in place with From, To, and What's moving preserved. Request a quote to confirm storage pricing for your dates and items.

2. Packing, room by room — full, partial, or fragile-only, plus unpacking at the other end. You may pack yourself; the company loads, moves, and places.

3. Loading, sequenced — heavy items low and first, boxes staged by room, fragile secured on top, everything strapped against movement.

4. Hold — items held in leased storage between move-out and move-in.

5. Redelivery — when the destination is ready, goods are redelivered and placed room by room, furniture reassembled, beds and wardrobes rebuilt.

6. Walkthrough — final walkthrough at placement.

The free video-walkthrough survey room is available: film only — never lift, move, open, or climb anything heavy or locked — with a human-made estimate.

## Storage, explained — industry background, not our terms

Everything in this section is general industry information from mover and regulator sources. It explains how storage works in general. It is NOT The Flat Rate Movers' storage terms: our storage terms — leased storage, any item type, 30-day minimum stay, customer access while stored, lease terms vary, and storage quoted per job, monthly, or by volume — are stated in the sections above.

### Storage types (industry)

Short-term storage covers days to weeks — closing gaps, overlapping leases. Long-term storage covers months to years — renovations, deployments, downsizing, estate transitions, staging. Containerized or vaulted storage packs belongings into sealed wooden vaults at the home, inventoried and stored intact, so they are handled less; one vault holds about one room, and one published vault size is 7.5' × 7' × 5', about 245 cubic feet. Storage-in-transit (SIT) is temporary warehouse storage during a move. Other industry forms include vehicle, boat, and RV storage; commercial storage for inventory, files, fixtures, FF&E, and records with chain-of-custody, plus receiving, staging, retail overflow, and seasonal inventory; fine art, antique, and high-value storage; and temperature- or climate-controlled storage.

### Storage-in-transit rules (industry, FMCSA / NCUC)

SIT is federally defined temporary warehouse storage during a move, capped at 180 days; after 180 days it converts to permanent storage under a separate warehouse contract, with written notice required covering the conversion date, a 9-month claim window, the end of transit liability, and the warehouseman's rules and charges. Under SIT, goods stay under the bill of lading and the valuation chosen for the move — Released Value at $0.60 per pound, with Full Value Protection available; after conversion, coverage shifts to warehouse-receipt terms. SIT rates are typically weight-based rather than per-container, billed in 30-day increments, sometimes prorated. One SIT rule matters for leased space: NCUC states SIT shipments must be held in a warehouse owned by the carrier or a public warehouse in which the carrier has a long-term lease agreement. We describe our storage as leased storage.

### Inventory and protection (industry practice)

Numbered tags with condition noted at load-in; furniture blanket-wrapped; mirrors and art boxed; mattresses and upholstery covered; goods palletized or vaulted; held in secured, access-controlled space; climate control for wood, electronics, and sensitive items. The same inventory governs release, with a tag check at redelivery.

### Access models (industry)

Business-hours access; advance notice of 24 hours or 48 hours in published examples; attendant-assisted access, sometimes at an hourly rate; partial retrieval of selected items, sometimes for a small handling fee. None of these is our rule — they are industry models, listed so the options are understood.

### Pricing models (industry figures only — never our prices)

Published figures from other movers, listed for education: SIT at $0.40–$0.75 per cubic foot per month plus about $75 per vault in each direction (one Florida source); vault storage at $85–$115 per vault per month (one California source); $85 per vault per month plus a $100 setup fee (one Massachusetts source); monthly pricing by home size from one New Jersey mover (studio $130–$250, 2-bedroom $250–$400, 3–4 bedroom $400–$650); self-storage 5×10 units at $60–$220 depending on market and climate control. Pricing drivers in the industry are volume, weight, or cubic footage; climate control; duration; and location. Month-to-month billing and multi-month discounts are individual movers' offers, not industry rules. No figure in this paragraph is The Flat Rate Movers' price.

### Typical exclusions (industry education only — not our list)

Other movers commonly exclude perishables, live plants and animals, flammables, fuel and chemicals, illegal substances, unlicensed firearms, and hazardous materials. That is industry practice. Our published scope statement is "any type of items" with the examples above.

### Climate rationale (industry)

Stable temperature and humidity protect wood furniture, electronics, books, photographs, and fabrics; one premium published example is 18–24°C with 40–60% humidity. This paragraph states industry rationale only.

## Junk removal, on stated terms

Junk removal clears the non-hazardous items a property no longer needs: furniture, appliances, mattresses and box springs, electronics, exercise equipment, hot tubs, yard debris, renovation debris, and the accumulated contents of garages, basements, attics, estates, evictions, and offices. Every job is surveyed first and quoted at one flat rate in writing — the full scope reviewed, the price set before work begins, never a clock. Hazardous and regulated waste is not taken: no wet paint or solvents, no fuels or motor oil, no chemicals or pesticides, no pressurized tanks, no asbestos-containing material, no medical or biohazard waste. Heavy pieces are not forced through this service — a gun safe or another high-mass asset of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs moves under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation, and pianos move under the piano, antique and white-glove service.

## Who it is for

This service is for anyone with a date and a property that has to be empty by it: homeowners clearing a house for a listing, a closing, or a move; downsizers and families sorting a household into keep, donate, and remove; estate executors clearing a whole property to a settlement deadline; landlords and property managers after an eviction or a turnover; renovators and contractors whose old kitchen, bathroom, flooring, or fixtures have to be out before the new work goes in; businesses clearing offices, retail fixtures, and warehouse corners; and households with one oversized problem — a hot tub, a dead refrigerator, a garage that stopped fitting a car years ago.

## What it includes

The lifting, carrying, and loading, from where the items sit — basements, attics, garages, upper floors, and yards. Floors, walls, and doorways on the path out are protected, pieces are carried and never dragged, and standard furniture is taken apart when a piece has to come apart to leave safely. Hot tub shells are cut and hauled in sections once the tub is drained and disconnected. After pickup, every load is sorted before anything is thrown out: usable goods are routed toward donation, recyclable materials toward recycling, appliances that contain refrigerant toward processing where certified technicians recover the refrigerant first, construction and demolition debris toward facilities that accept it, and only the remainder toward a transfer station or landfill. The job ends with a walkthrough of the cleared space.

## How it works

1. Survey — items are inventoried where they sit, with room, floor, and access noted, in person or through the free film-only video walkthrough survey room.

2. Flat-rate quote — the full scope of the job is reviewed — the items, the distance, the manpower, and the equipment — and priced at one flat rate in writing before work begins. Nothing is auto-priced, and hourly pricing is available when a client asks for it.

3. Scheduling — the removal is set against your date: the closing, the turnover, the project start, the settlement deadline.

4. Removal — the crew lifts, carries, and loads from where items sit, protecting the path out, and takes standard pieces apart when a piece must come apart to leave safely.

5. Sorting and routing — the load is sorted after pickup: usable goods toward donation, recyclables toward recycling, regulated-stream items toward the facilities that handle them, the remainder to lawful disposal.

6. Walkthrough — final walkthrough of the cleared space; nothing in the surveyed scope is left behind.

The free video-walkthrough survey room is available: film only — never lift, move, open, or climb anything heavy or locked — with a human-made estimate.

## Junk removal, explained — industry background, not our terms

Everything in this section is general industry information from hauler, pricing-guide, and regulator sources. It explains how junk removal works in general. It is NOT The Flat Rate Movers' terms: our terms — surveyed in advance, one flat rate in writing before work begins, hourly pricing is available when a client asks for it, hazardous and regulated waste not taken — are stated in the sections above.

### Pricing models (industry figures only — never our prices)

Most of the industry prices by truck volume, in fractions of a load: a minimum pickup, then quarter, half, three-quarter, and full truckloads, in trucks of roughly 15–18 cubic yards. Published 2026 U.S. pricing guides put typical ranges at roughly $70–$175 for a minimum pickup, $150–$300 for a quarter load, $250–$550 for a half load, and $550–$1,000 for a full truckload (Housecall Pro and MyQuoteIQ 2026 guides). Other haulers price by weight per ton, by the item for single pickups, or by the hour at published guide rates of $50–$150 — the hourly model is the one whose price is not known until the job is done. The industry's cost drivers are volume, weight and density (disposal facilities bill haulers by weight), labor and access (stairs, long carries, disassembly), distance, and the disposal fees the load itself carries. No figure in this paragraph is The Flat Rate Movers' price: our price for a job is the written flat rate for that job.

### What haulers take, and what they leave (industry)

Across the industry, standard junk removal takes most non-hazardous household and commercial items — furniture, mattresses, appliances, electronics, exercise equipment, hot tubs, yard debris, office contents, and renovation material — and does not take hazardous or regulated material: wet paint, solvents, gasoline and motor oil, pesticides and household chemicals, propane and other pressurized tanks, asbestos-containing material, and medical or biohazard waste, all of which route to licensed handlers or household hazardous waste facilities. Gray-area items in the industry include tires, lead-acid batteries, fluorescent tubes, and older cathode-ray-tube screens, which need special handling streams. Our own take and no-take lists are the ones stated above.

### The refrigerant rule (federal)

Refrigerators, freezers, and air conditioners contain refrigerant. Under Section 608 of the Clean Air Act (40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F), knowingly venting refrigerant is prohibited, and refrigerant must be recovered with certified equipment by Section 608-certified technicians before a refrigerant-bearing appliance is disposed of or processed. In practice, haulers route these appliances to processing where that recovery happens. This company claims no refrigerant-recovery certification; the rule is stated here because it governs where a refrigerator can lawfully go after pickup.

### After the truck leaves (industry practice)

On a well-run job, a hauled load is sorted before anything is thrown out, because once items are crushed together in a compactor nothing can be salvaged. The first pass pulls anything still usable — furniture with life left in it, working appliances, tools, household goods — toward donation channels and thrift reuse. The second pass separates materials recyclers take: scrap metal (graded and weighed as ferrous and non-ferrous), cardboard, clean wood, and electronics for e-waste recycling. A third pass isolates items that need special handling streams, such as refrigerant appliances and mattresses. What survives all three passes as genuinely spent goes to a transfer station or landfill. Published industry writing describes diversion this way as practice, with no single rate applying to every load — and this page claims no donation or diversion percentage for this company.

### Dense debris and weight (industry)

Bulky and dense are different problems. A sofa fills truck space and weighs little; concrete, brick, soil, and roofing fill little space and weigh a great deal — and because disposal is billed by weight and trucks have legal weight limits, dense debris governs how much can ride in one load and is priced accordingly across the industry. That is why a surveyed scope, not a guess over the phone, is what a serious price is written against.

### Mattresses and bulky items (industry)

Mattresses are the classic awkward load: bulky, low-density, and unwelcome at many facilities, which often charge per-unit handling for them; some regions run dedicated mattress recycling programs that strip them into steel, foam, and fiber. Hot tubs are the other classic: drained and disconnected from power and water first, then cut into sections small enough to carry. Both are routine for a removal crew — and both are exactly the kind of item a survey prices correctly and a guess prices wrong.

## Questions, answered

What does junk removal include?

The lifting, carrying, and loading of non-hazardous items from where they sit, the haul-away, the sorting of the load after pickup — usable goods toward donation, recyclables toward recycling — and lawful disposal of the remainder, ending with a walkthrough of the cleared space.

How much does junk removal cost?

Each job is priced at one flat rate in writing after a survey of the full scope — there is no rate card and no published hourly price. The industry mostly prices by truck volume, and published guide ranges for that model are in "Junk removal, explained" above, labeled as industry figures. Our price for your job is the written flat rate for your job.

How is the flat rate set?

We review the full scope of each job — the items, the distance, the manpower, and the equipment — and give a flat rate, as opposed to an hourly rate. Access found at the survey (stairs, long carries, a hot tub to section) is inside the price, not added on the day.

What items do you take?

Furniture, appliances, mattresses and box springs, electronics, exercise equipment, hot tubs, yard debris, renovation debris (drywall, lumber, flooring, cabinets, fixtures), bagged household junk, and whole-property cleanout contents from homes, estates, evictions, and businesses.

What items can you not take?

Hazardous and regulated waste: wet paint and solvents, fuels and motor oil, pesticides and household chemicals, pressurized tanks, asbestos-containing material, lead paint material, and medical or biohazard waste. Those belong to licensed handlers and household hazardous waste routes.

Do you remove hot tubs?

Yes. The tub is drained and disconnected from power and water before the appointment; the crew then cuts the shell and hauls it out in sections.

Do you take refrigerators and other appliances?

Yes — washers, dryers, ranges, dishwashers, refrigerators, freezers, and water heaters. Appliances that contain refrigerant are routed to processing where certified technicians recover the refrigerant before the appliance is processed, as federal rules require.

Do you do estate and eviction cleanouts?

Yes — whole-property cleanouts for estates, evictions, foreclosures, and turnovers, surveyed as one scope and priced at one flat rate for the whole property.

Do you take construction or renovation debris?

Yes — drywall, lumber, flooring, carpet, cabinets, countertops, and fixtures from renovation work. Dense material such as concrete, brick, and soil is planned by weight, because weight governs how much a truck can carry in one load.

What happens to my junk after pickup?

The load is sorted before anything is thrown out. Usable goods are routed toward donation, recyclable materials toward recycling, regulated-stream items toward the facilities that handle them, and only the remainder goes to a transfer station or landfill.

What if the junk includes a safe or a piano?

Those are not forced through junk removal. A gun safe or another high-mass asset of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs moves under Structural Integrity Relocation (SIR), with floor deflection analysis to L/360; a piano moves under the piano, antique and white-glove service. Ask about the piece when you request your quote and it is routed to the right service.

## Racking relocation, on stated terms

When a warehouse moves, the racking is the part nobody owns. The rack dealer sells steel and installation. A mover sells transport. In between, the teardown, the labeling, the inventory on the steel, the weeks the new building is not ready, and the reinstall fall to whoever the operations manager can find — usually an out-of-state install crew that will not touch the inventory, or a moving crew that has never taken a bay apart. This service closes that gap: The Flat Rate Movers tears down, transports, stages and reinstalls pallet racking, and moves the inventory that sits on it, as one job under one flat rate. Every job is surveyed first and quoted in writing — the full scope reviewed, the price set before work begins, never a clock, never an automatic estimate.

The scope is stated as plainly as the boundaries. Our crews perform the physical work end to end — teardown, transport, storage staging, reinstallation and anchoring to the floor — to the manufacturer's specification and ANSI MH16.1 / RMI guidance, with anchor type, size and torque set by the project's Load Application and Rack Configuration (LARC) drawings. Where a project requires engineering, seismic calculation or permits, we consult and arrange them through the certified contractors we engage: the sealed drawings, the racking permit and any high-pile storage approval are their work, issued by the local authority having jurisdiction, and they are handled inside your one flat-rate engagement — you never have to source a separate engineer to get the job done. We hold no engineering license or permit authority ourselves, and we say so on this page. Components found bent or damaged at teardown are set aside and reported to you in writing. They are never re-erected. That rule is a safety practice, and it is on this page because it should be asked of anyone who quotes this work.

## Who it is for

This service is for the people who own a warehouse move date. Warehouse and distribution-center operations managers whose real cost is downtime and whose real fear is a teardown that loses parts, labels or sequence. 3PL site managers whose client contracts start and end on dates the racking has to match. Industrial property and facilities managers handling a lease surrender, a consolidation, or an expansion. General contractors and fit-out project managers who need a disassembly and reassembly crew that plugs into a construction schedule instead of competing with it. Racking dealers and installers who sell the steel and the engineering and need a teardown, transport and reinstall crew in the I-81 corridor. And office and corporate facilities managers buying the other half of this category: cubicle and systems-furniture teardown and reassembly for office moves, renovations and reconfigurations. If your project is a set of trained, supervised, self-managed teams on a job rather than individual temp labor, this is the same workforce that runs our industrial and commercial project support — engaged per job, with no required contract duration.

## What it includes

Scope | What happens |

Pallet rack teardown | Beams, decking and frames come down in sequence; every component labeled to its bay and level; the hardware — anchor bolts, beam safety clips and pins, shims — bagged and counted per bay; condition inspected as it comes down. |

Inventory move-off and return | Product pulled, palletized, stretch-wrapped and counted before the steel moves; put back on the racking in the planned sequence at the destination, counts reconciled. |

Transport | Steel and inventory move together on the company's trucks — frames nested, beams bundled, hardware traveling with its bay — in phased loads where the destination is built out in zones. |

Storage staging | Racking and inventory held in the company's leased storage space when the destination is not ready: 30-day minimum, customer access, priced per job, monthly, or by volume. |

Reinstallation | Frames set, leveled, plumbed and anchored to the floor at the destination by our crews, to the manufacturer's specification and the project's engineered drawings, following ANSI MH16.1 / RMI guidance — wedge anchors of the type and size the project's LARC drawings specify, beam safety clips or pins set at every connection, base plates shimmed level, wire decking and pallet supports laid back in, column protectors and row spacers refitted; beam levels set to plan; load plaques posted for the as-built configuration. |

Reconfiguration | Beam-level changes and row re-layout inside the same building — the system comes apart and goes back together around a new inventory profile without leaving the site. |

Decommissioning | Full teardown and removal at lease end, including anchor grinding and filling where your lease requires the slab returned. |

Industrial equipment D&R | Production and line equipment broken into transportable sections, skidded or crated where needed, transported, set in place and leveled at destination. Single pieces of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs move under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol, with an L/360 floor-deflection check. |

Office-systems D&R | Cubicle and systems-furniture teardown, transport and reassembly — panels, worksurfaces, overhead storage and pedestals — for office moves and renovations. Licensed-trade electrical and building data work stays with your contractor's trades. |

The rack types this work covers, in the vocabulary your survey will use:

Selective pallet rackThe single-deep beam-and-upright default — most of the racking in most warehouses, and the bulk of relocation work.
Double-deep rackTwo pallets deep per side; reach-truck access; beam levels and lane labels carry the sequence.
Drive-in / drive-through rackHigh-density lanes the forklift enters; last-in, first-out; rail and upright condition is checked closely at teardown.
Pushback rackCarts on inclined rails, two to six pallets deep; carts and rails are matched sets and are labeled to stay together.
Pallet-flow rackGravity roller lanes, first-in, first-out; rollers and speed controllers are inventoried per lane.
Cantilever rackArms off a central column for long loads — lumber, pipe, bar stock. Governed by ANSI MH16.3, a separate standard from the MH16.1 that covers beam rack.
Carton-flow and pick modulesCase-flow lanes and multi-level pick structures, including mezzanine-supported rack.

## What we do for you

You get one accountable crew for the part of a warehouse move that usually takes three vendors and a spreadsheet of finger-pointing. The survey documents your system where it stands — manufacturer, bay counts, beam levels, elevations, decking, anchors, condition — and surveys the destination against it, so the layout question is answered before the first beam drops, not after the steel is on a truck. Inventory is sequenced off the racking in the order your restart needs it, counted at the door the way our transloading floor counts freight. Teardown labels every component to its bay and level, because a rack that arrives as anonymous steel is a second project, not a moved one. If the new building is not ready, the steel and the inventory stage in storage instead of in a parking lot. And the reinstall is finished work: level, plumb, anchored to the floor, plaques posted, counts reconciled, and the damaged pieces accounted for in writing instead of quietly loaded at the back of a row.
