- **Asset & Structure Assessment Operations** — Asset and structure assessment operations — the survey that gates every SIR move. Published asset inputs: weight, dimensions, centre of mass, and value at risk, with calibration-sensitive and fragile items flagged at the assess stage. Published structure inputs: the route and clearance at both ends, stairs and landings measured, the substrate, and floor deflection assessed against L/360 — span divided by 360 — before any lift is planned; the plan outputs are the load path, the spreading and protection runs, and the crew and rigging matched to the plan. The company's published rule is that the building is assessed before the asset moves: every SIR move starts with the building, not the item. Domain education, labeled as such and never a company figure: L/360 is the standard residential floor deflection limit in the IRC framework (Table R502.3.1) — a 10-foot span may deflect about one-third of an inch, a 12-foot span 0.40 inches, a 15-foot span 0.50 inches — and tile and stone floors demand the stricter L/480. IRC design loads are 40 psf live load in living areas, 30 psf in sleeping areas, and 20 psf in uninhabitable attic storage, plus roughly 10 to 20 psf dead load, all as uniform loads; a heavy asset concentrates its weight on a small footprint, which is why the published method checks the structure first. Not published and not claimed: any PSI value, floor-load figure, or joist schedule as company engineering data, and any involvement of a licensed structural engineer. Download: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-sir-heavy.json · Landing: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/sir-heavy/
- **The Flat Rate Movers — Virginia Inland Port Transloading Process Chain Dataset** — The published process chain for a container worked through the inland port layer, anchored to how freight actually arrives in the Valley. Arrival: the container reaches the corridor by Norfolk Southern rail through the Virginia Inland Port ramp at Front Royal, or by truck on I-81, I-66 or I-70, and the turn is planned as a scheduled operation inside the carrier's free time, because an unplanned queue at the door is where demurrage and detention clocks start. Seal and paperwork: the seal number is checked against the shipping documents before the container is opened, and exceptions — short counts, seal mismatches, damage — are documented at intake, not discovered at delivery (domain reference, general industry practice, labeled as such, and already published in the generic process chain). Devanning: floor-loaded freight is unloaded piece by piece and palletized freight is pulled by forklift, counted against the paperwork and checked as it crosses the dock. Deconsolidation: one container is split into many outbound loads, sorted by destination, order, SKU, store, site or region. Cross-dock or stage: straight-through freight passes from inbound to outbound without storage; freight held for timed release is staged by destination until its window — staging is a defined state, not a default. Rework: damaged or shifted loads are reported and reworked on the floor, not passed on — salvageable freight separated, counted and restacked; repalletizing onto sound pallets, rewrapping in stretch wrap, bracing and banding, and relabeling; and tarping or re-tarping, where an open-deck load is covered, re-covered or re-secured during rework so it leaves weather-tight (the rework line for tarping is defined in the taxonomy node of this dataset file). The materials the work consumes — tarps and tie-downs, stretch wrap, pallets, banding, labels and markers — are purchased for each project and scoped inside the job’s flat rate. Outbound build: loads are built into 53 ft domestic trailers, less-than-truckload or full-truckload runs, or handed to final-mile delivery; the standard inland saving is the consolidation of three 40 ft ocean containers of light, floor-loaded freight into two 53 ft domestic trailers (industry rule of thumb, not a guaranteed ratio). Empty turn: empties are turned around instead of sitting, closing the free-time loop. Export loads run the chain in reverse — received, packed and braced, crated to ISPM 15 where the shipment needs it, and loaded for the port leg through the inland port to Hampton Roads. Download: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-transloading-inland-port.json · Landing: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/transloading-inland-port/
- **Cross-Dock, Decon & Restack Operations** — Cross-dock, deconsolidation, and restack operations for Winchester transloading — the dwell models and the restack arithmetic, as data. Cross-dock: freight never enters storage and leaves the same shift. Deconsolidation: the container is broken by destination, purchase order, or SKU. Restack: freight is rebuilt into 53ft domestic trailers, split across destinations where the job calls for it. Restack arithmetic, labeled domain-typical and governed by each load plan: a 40ft container fills about 20 pallet positions; a 20ft about 10. Dwell models, labeled domain: cross-dock dwell is measured in hours; storage between legs is measured in days. IPI — where the original container continues inland intact — is vocabulary in this dataset, not a Winchester service claim. Outbound modes recorded as data: full truckload, less-than-truckload, and split delivery. No dwell-time guarantee and no rate of any kind is published in this dataset. Download: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-transloading-winchester.json · Landing: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/transloading-winchester/
- **The Flat Rate Movers — Transloading Process Chain Dataset** — The published process chain for a transloaded container on the company's warehouse floor, defined step by step on the service's docs page: receive the container; unload — floor-loaded by hand, palletised by forklift; count against the paperwork; sort by destination, order or SKU; stage; palletise, wrap and label the outbound loads; then transload onward or hand off to final-mile delivery. At the container door (published): floor-loaded freight is unloaded piece by piece, counted and staged; palletised freight is pulled, checked and restacked; damaged or shifted loads are reported and reworked on the floor, not passed on. Export loads run the chain in reverse — packed, braced and loaded for the port leg, with ISPM 15 crating where the shipment needs it. Staging is a defined state, not a default: freight that should not sit does not sit (cross-dock), and freight held for timed release is staged by destination until its window. Domain reference (general industry practice, labeled as such): the seal number is checked against the shipping documents before a container is opened; freight is captured in a warehouse management system at intake; exceptions — short counts, seal mismatches, damage — are documented at intake, not discovered at delivery; and a transload turn is planned as a scheduled operation inside the carrier's free time, because an unplanned queue at the door is where demurrage and detention clocks start. Download: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-transloading.json · Landing: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/transloading/
- **Vault Door Freight Recovery Case Study — Manassas, VA (September 2026)** — The structured case record of one real vault door job, published as data: in September 2026 a reconditioned vault door — 1,475 lbs on one pallet at 41 × 41 × 42 inches, cube 40.86 cubic feet, density 36.1 PCF, freight class 60, NMFC 172360-11, prepaid — was shipped by LTL freight to a carrier terminal in Manassas, VA and held will-call. The Flat Rate Movers' Winchester branch crew recovered it at the loading dock inside the 7:30 AM – 2:00 PM pickup window, ran the final-mile leg to the client, and placed the door under the white-glove standard. The dataset carries the complete end-to-end process as seven structured steps, each mapped to the registered service that performed it, the full transcribed freight record, and the evidence block: the document types and dates behind every figure, with the density cross-check (1,475 lbs ÷ 40.86 cu ft = 36.1 PCF) verified against the bill of lading. Names of individuals, the seller and the client are withheld under the company's privacy rule; geography is published at city level. Download: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-vault-door-case-study.json · Landing: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/vault-door-case-study/
- **Vault Door Models — Verified Manufacturer Data** — Verified manufacturer data for vault door models — the doors a relocation or installation is planned from. The population carries 8 models from 3 manufacturers (Liberty Safe, Fort Knox, Overly Door Company), with manufacturer-stated weights from 1,225 to 1,610 lbs; 2 of the weighed models fall inside the SIR band of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs. Every row states only what the manufacturer's own documents state: where a manufacturer does not publish a clear opening, a thickness, or a model price, the field is absent from the row and the reason is recorded on the row. The dataset grows by verified rows only; its count is the count the verification protocol has passed, stated as it stands. Download: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-vault-doors.json · Landing: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/vault-doors/
- **Vault Door Standards Registry — UL 608, AA-D-600D, FF-L-2740B** — The verified standards registry for vault doors and high-security enclosures. UL 608 classes M, 1, 2, and 3 carry net working times of 15, 30, 60, and 120 minutes against one identical attack basis — common mechanical tools, electric tools, cutting torches, or any combination — and UL 608 section 1.3 excludes attack with the burning bar (thermal lance) or explosives from every class. GSA Class 5-V under AA-D-600D requires resistance to 20 man-hours of surreptitious entry, 30 man-minutes of covert entry, and 10 man-minutes of forced entry, with no ballistic requirement; Class 5-A drops the surreptitious requirement; Class 5-B adds ballistic resistance tested to SD-STD-01.01 Rev. G level 2, and the specification names no test round. Door lock requirements are recorded as their own fields, never blended into the door figures: Class 5-V and 5-B doors carry a lock meeting FF-L-2740 (Style H or K), while Class 5-A's lock is a UL 768 Group 1 lock. The registry also carries three corrective notes where widely published charts contradict the standards' own text. Every row carries the primary source it was verified against on 2026-11-02. Download: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-vault-security.json · Landing: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/vault-security/
- **The Flat Rate Movers — Moving Videos Dataset** — The published video dataset of The Flat Rate Movers: the six VideoObject records behind the estate’s Videos page — DMV Moving Made Easy: Top-Rated Movers in Winchester & Beyond! (#WinchesterVA #MoversVA #DMVMovers); Moving a Heavy Gun Safe? We Can Help! Flat Rate Movers (VA); The Flat Rate Movers of Winchester: Safe and Reliable Gun Safe Moving in Northern Virginia; Final Mile Delivery & White Glove Safe Installation | 1,800 lb Locker System (Full Process); Medical Tank Relocation: Experts for Your Sensitive Equipment; Gun Safe Movers Moving a 900 lb Gun Safe BROWNING PROSTEEL 1878 SERIES — published as structured data under CC BY 4.0 so search and AI systems read the same titles and descriptions the Videos page serves. Download: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-videos.json · Landing: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/videos/
- **The Flat Rate Movers — Racking Relocation Process Chain Dataset** — The published process chain for a racking relocation, step by step: (1) Survey and inventory — the existing system is documented where it stands: manufacturer and component types, bay counts, beam levels and elevations, upright heights and depths, decking, anchors and condition; the destination is surveyed against it for ceiling height, column spacing, slab and dock access; damaged or bent components are flagged at this step, not discovered at reinstall. (2) Sequencing plan — inventory comes off the steel in a planned order, by SKU velocity, destination zone or restart priority; the teardown sequence, the labeling scheme and the destination layout on the project's engineered drawings are confirmed before the first beam drops. (3) Inventory move-off — product is pulled, palletized, stretch-wrapped and counted, and either moved to its destination zones or staged in storage; counts are checked against the paperwork at the door, the same count discipline the transloading floor runs. (4) Teardown — beams, decking and frames come down in sequence; every component is labeled to its bay and level; hardware — anchor bolts, beam safety clips and pins, shims — is bagged and counted per bay; components are inspected as they come down, and damaged or bent uprights are set aside and reported, never re-erected. (5) Transport — steel and inventory move together on the company's trucks, frames nested, beams bundled, hardware traveling with its bay; phased loads where the destination is built out in zones. (6) Storage staging, where the timeline needs it — racking and inventory held in leased storage space (30-day minimum, customer access) when the destination is not ready. (7) Reinstall — frames set, leveled, plumbed and anchored to the floor at the destination by the company's crews — wedge anchors of the type and size the project's LARC drawings specify, safety clips or pins at every beam connection, base plates shimmed level, wire decking, pallet supports, column protectors and row spacers refitted — to the manufacturer's specification and the project's engineered drawings, following ANSI MH16.1 / RMI guidance; the project's LARC drawings govern anchor type, size and torque; beam levels set to plan; load plaques posted for the as-built configuration. (8) Closeout — inventory goes back on the steel in sequence, counts reconcile, the as-built bay map is handed over, and set-aside components are accounted for in writing. Project management is the method inside the chain — survey, inventory, sequence, cutover, closeout — not a separate service sold on its own. Download: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-warehouse-racking-relocation.json · Landing: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/warehouse-racking-relocation/
- **Facility & Access Operations** — Facility and access operations for warehouse relocation. Published site inputs: the job is scoped around the site itself — access, floor space, staging, and equipment handling. Dispatch network: the Winchester, VA and Martinsburg, WV branches, along the I-81, I-66, and I-70 corridors, across the Shenandoah Valley and the Eastern Panhandle. Facility types seen across the market, labeled domain context: distribution centers and 3PL facilities; manufacturing warehouses; retail and e-commerce fulfillment sites; cold and climate-controlled facilities; records, FF&E, and project staging space. Access inputs used in industry move planning, labeled domain only: dock times and access at both facilities; gate and security coordination; clearances; floor-loading realities; ceiling heights; power points; aisle widths for equipment; warehouse-system internet live on day one. Building-compliance topics from domain practice, labeled as such: high-piled storage permits; seismic permits (a California example); fire-code compliance on reinstall; anchor patterns around post-tension slab mapping; sprinkler and flue-space constraints. Beyond the published site inputs, no dock-scheduling, gate-coordination, clearance-survey, permit, or engineering offering is published or claimed for this company. Download: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-warehouse.json · Landing: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/warehouse/
- **The Flat Rate Movers — White-Glove Delivery Process Chain Dataset** — The process chain for a white-glove delivery, as published on the service's hub page. Step 1, name the pieces: the client names the pieces, and each piece is assessed on its own — weight, fragile points, finish and value at risk. Step 2, match the protection: padded blankets and clear stretch wrap as the standard, a custom crate built around the piece when it needs more; high-mass pieces are surveyed and floor-checked to L/360 under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol before they move. Step 3, receive and stage: freight arriving through the freight chain is unloaded on the warehouse floor, counted and inventoried as it crosses the dock, and staged for the delivery — deconsolidated or cross-docked where a shipment needs to split or change vehicles, and reworked where needed. Step 4, deliver in on a planned route: the item crosses the threshold — never left at a curb — to homes, offices, industrial sites and retail. Step 5, place: the item is set in its final position, where it belongs. Step 6, remove packaging: the delivered item's packaging is removed, so the recipient is not left with the wrap and the boxes. Step 7, verify: placement and condition are verified with the recipient before the crew leaves. Domain reference (the general delivered-in sequence, labeled as such): appointment scheduling with the recipient and a pre-delivery access check — doorways, stairs, elevators — belong to the same chain in the industry's general practice; the company's published chain above is the company's own, and its deliveries are arranged by appointment, set when the job is scoped and quoted. Download: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-white-glove.json · Landing: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/white-glove/

The search-intent rubric (datasets-intent-coverage.json) maps 26,245 buyer-intent queries to the page, per-page JSON, dataset and graph node that answer each one, covering all 264 pages of the estate.

Page Data: every one of the 264 pages also carries two data files beside it — data.json (machine) and data.txt (plain text) — drawn mechanically from the Page Data Pool (datasets-page-data-pool.json) under draw rules DR-1..DR-11: the page's scope offered and not offered, sourced qualifiers, audiences, geography, and its buyer questions with alternate phrasings, answers and section evidence. Each page's head block names the two files and carries their SHA-256 digests; both files are signed distributions. The API serves the inventory at https://api.theflatratemovers.com/v1/page-data and one page's record at /v1/page-data/{slug}. Rubric scores for every page: https://theflatratemovers.com/page-data-scores.json (all pages at 100/100; a page under 100 fails its seal).

Every file above — and every page of the site — is a sealed distribution in the signed AI master index: 1161 distributions in total after the 2026-10-31 per-route batch.

## Certificate — how to verify

Every published file of this estate is sealed in a signed index. To verify any file:

1. Fetch the signing key (Ed25519, key id theflatratemovers-2026-10-29-1): https://theflatratemovers.com/.well-known/signing-keys.json — SHA-256 fingerprint k_HfnSkokedjQMSjLj-X8ftw40CUr92dBgecXsP14y4 (as published in llms.txt).
2. Fetch the signed index: https://theflatratemovers.com/ai-master-index.json and its detached-style JWS: https://theflatratemovers.com/ai-master-index.jws (EdDSA over the RFC 8785 canonical form of the index).
3. Find the file’s distribution entry by contentUrl and compare the SHA-256 digest of the bytes you fetched with the entry’s digest. A match proves the bytes are the estate’s published bytes, unaltered.

# Developer resources — the machine-readable site.
This page is for developers, search and AI systems, and technical partners working with The Flat Rate Movers data: our business facts are published as structured data at the highest level — JSON-LD on every page of this site, plus live JSON and text endpoints that all say the same founding, geo, hours, services and service areas.

Get My Flat Rate Quote (#/quote)

### Live API — api.theflatratemovers.com
The Flat Rate Movers publishes a live, read-only API for AI systems, search engines and developers at https://api.theflatratemovers.com (https://api.theflatratemovers.com). It serves all 33 services (/v1/services), the 39 published dataset files byte-identical to this site (/v1/datasets), the search-intent rubric (/v1/intent), the entity graph (/v1/graph), the signed master index (/v1/index) and signed-index verification (/v1/verify) — every response traceable to the signed provenance index at ai-master-index.json (/ai-master-index.json) (Ed25519, key id theflatratemovers-2026-10-29-1). An MCP server for agent tools is at https://api.theflatratemovers.com/mcp (https://api.theflatratemovers.com/mcp) (tools: search_intent, get_service, get_dataset, verify_file, list_services, list_datasets). The datasets are also mirrored on Hugging Face (huggingface.co/datasets/theflatratemovers (https://huggingface.co/datasets/theflatratemovers)) and archived on Zenodo under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23818766 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23818766).

The dataset collection itself — the files behind this site — was deposited at Zenodo on November 2, 2026 under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23879048 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23879048). The announcement tells the whole story: The Flat Rate Movers publish their dataset estate with a citable DOI (#/flat-rate-movers-dataset-estate-citable-doi).

### Packing data

### Signed machine data
Every file in the AI master index carries a SHA-256 digest of the exact bytes served, and the index itself is signed with the company’s Ed25519 key — published at /.well-known/signing-keys.json → (/.well-known/signing-keys.json) (key id theflatratemovers-2026-10-29-1). Verify the signature over the canonical index (ai-master-index.jws → (/ai-master-index.jws)), then recompute any file’s digest to prove it is genuine and unaltered. Since 2026-10-30 the seal covers the whole estate: all 205 per-page JSON files, the site shell, and the deployed code — the Pages functions, the quote-form Worker source, and the Machine’s own verification tools — are signed distributions alongside the dataset packs, 260 distributions in all. Master index: ai-master-index.json → (/ai-master-index.json).

### About this page

This page covers Live endpoints, On-page structured data, Go deeper — from The Flat Rate Movers, quoted at one flat rate in writing before move day, under the guarantee: Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free! Where the topic is a heavy or high-value move, it is planned under SIR and the KIM-GS Protocol, for assets of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs with an L/360 floor check, and where it is an export or freight topic, packing and crating are to ISPM 15.

From Winchester, VA (116 W Piccadilly St Suite 11, Mon–Fri 8am–6pm, Sat 8am–4pm, Sun 9am–4pm) and Martinsburg, WV (736 Williamsport Pike Suite 2, Mon–Fri 9am–6pm, Sat 9am–4pm, Sun 9am–4pm), phone +1-540-422-2153, email ratemovers@gmail.com. Get a flat rate quote for the job itself, Short or Detailed, with From, To and What is moving preserved when you switch.

- GET https://api.theflatratemovers.com/v1/services — all 34 services
- GET https://api.theflatratemovers.com/v1/datasets — the 49 published dataset files, byte-identical to this site
- GET https://api.theflatratemovers.com/v1/intent — the search-intent rubric as data
- GET https://api.theflatratemovers.com/v1/graph — the entity graph
- GET https://api.theflatratemovers.com/v1/index — the signed master index
- GET https://api.theflatratemovers.com/v1/verify?file=<filename> — live SHA-256 check of any file against the signed index
- GET https://api.theflatratemovers.com/v1/answer-evidence — the answer-engine evidence dataset

- POST https://api.theflatratemovers.com/mcp — MCP server (tools: search_intent, get_service, get_dataset, verify_file, list_services, list_datasets)
The datasets are also mirrored on Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/datasets/theflatratemovers) and archived on Zenodo under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23818766.

### WebMCP tools (registered on the website for agent browsers)

- `search_services` — Search the moving and logistics services The Flat Rate Movers publishes — residential, commercial and office moving, long-distance, gun safes and SIR heavy assets (1,500–3,500 lbs), pianos and antiques, ISPM 15 export packing and custom crating, transloading, final-mile delivery, data center and medical/lab relocation, warehouse racking, FF&E, workforce project support, junk removal, storage and more. Returns matching services with their canonical page URLs. Read-only: it changes nothing.
- `get_service` — Get the full published detail for one service of The Flat Rate Movers by its service id (from search_services): its name, type, canonical page, full description, the datasets that document it, and how many search-intent rows point at it. Read-only.
- `list_service_areas` — Look up where The Flat Rate Movers works: the published two-branch footprint (71 GeoJSON areas — Winchester, VA and Martinsburg, WV branches, 14 areas shared). With a place name, returns the matching areas and which branch serves each; with no input, returns the full footprint summary and every area name. The branches are distinct and are never blended. Read-only.
- `find_dataset` — Find the published machine-readable datasets of The Flat Rate Movers (32 files: operations, taxonomy, commercial terms, buyer personas, compliance and coverage per service family, plus the search-intent coverage dataset). Returns each match with its human landing page, its direct download URL and its SHA-256 digest from the signed index. All datasets are CC BY 4.0. Read-only.
- `search_intent` — Search The Flat Rate Machine's intent rubric: published rows that map real customer questions to the exact page that answers them, each row carrying its certificate fingerprints and an outcome record across the gates (crawled, indexed, understood, corroborated, cited-and-maintained). Use it to find which page answers a question, or to audit coverage by service or area. Read-only.
- `verify_certificate` — Verify one of The Flat Rate Movers' published files against the company's signed AI master index (Ed25519 certificate, key id theflatratemovers-2026-10-29-1): the live file is re-hashed at request time and compared with the digest the certificate carries. Returns whether they match. Read-only.
- `get_quote_guidance` — Explain how getting a flat rate quote from The Flat Rate Movers works: the Short (Quick Quote) and Detailed Project forms, what a person must provide, and what happens after they submit. Information only — this tool cannot request a quote, and no agent can submit the quote form; the person always completes and submits it themselves.

## How to cite

The search-intent dataset is archived on Zenodo under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23818766 (record: https://zenodo.org/records/23844324); cite the concept DOI for the dataset series. The estate datasets collection is archived as a dataset deposit under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23879048 (record: https://zenodo.org/records/23879049, Wikidata Q141969285); cite that DOI for the collection as a whole. The company is Wikidata Q141969215 and the book The Strategic Integrator is Wikidata Q141969268; the branches are OpenStreetMap nodes https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/14340286372 (Winchester) and https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/14340286373 (Martinsburg).
